title: Concrete or Pavers? How to Choose for Your Ohio Driveway
excerpt: Both last decades when they are installed right. The decision usually comes down to budget, repairs and the look you want in front of your home.
author: Maxima Concrete

body.text: Almost every driveway estimate we write starts with the same question: should it be poured concrete or pavers? There is no universal answer. Both surfaces last for decades when the base is right — and both fail early when it is not. What changes is the up-front cost, how repairs work, and how the finished driveway looks from the street.

A poured driveway is a single slab. It is the more affordable of the two per square foot, it is easy to clear in winter, and with a 6.5-bag mix, fiber mesh and 10-gauge wire mesh it handles Ohio freeze-thaw cycles well. The trade-off is repairs: because the slab is continuous, fixing a damaged area usually means cutting out and replacing a section, and a patch rarely matches the original color exactly.

A paver driveway is built from separate units set over a compacted base and bedding layer. That structure is the main advantage — if a section settles or a paver is damaged, the affected pieces can be lifted and reset without touching the rest of the driveway. Pavers also give you far more freedom in color, pattern and border detail, which is why they show up on homes where the driveway is part of the architecture.

items: Budget: concrete costs less to install; pavers cost more up front and less to repair over time.
Repairs: pavers can be lifted and reset; concrete is patched or partially replaced.
Look: concrete offers finishes and color; pavers offer patterns, borders and stone textures.
Snow: both handle plowing when properly installed, though poured concrete is the simpler surface to scrape.

body.text: Whichever surface you pick, the base under it decides how long it lasts. Concrete has almost no tolerance for uneven support — if the ground settles, the slab bridges the gap and cracks. Pavers move with the ground, but only if the base was compacted and graded correctly in the first place. When you compare estimates, ask what goes under the surface, not just what goes on top.
If you want the two options priced side by side for your property, we can walk the site and put both on paper.
